A dog food company records data on the number of dogs $(x)$ sheltered at some kennels across the country and the corresponding amount of dog food $y$ (in kilograms) consumed in a month. The scatter plot for the data and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above. 

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted data point?
question.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(10,175).$ So, our actual value is $y=175.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=10$ has the $y$-coordinate $200.$ So, our estimated value is $\overset{^}{y}=200.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225232/assets/2cd59a9ae9c7ad474a9d5a308d4b8f3c9b96be70acdf1e3613dfc4757ff01766.png)

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =175-200 \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residual is $-25\,kg.$
